content.text:
Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Fix GitHub issue #185 in the Moneo repo, together with the Home layout shift it likely shares a cause with. Your checkout is a new worktree on top of branch `t3/qa-stack` (PR #187), which adds a separate test backend. Read `AGENTS.md` fully first, especially **Safety**, **Test backend** and **Tests**, and follow them.

## Safety (hard rules)
- Never touch the owner's setup: their `.env`, Docker project `moneo`, or the app on port 3000. Never run `npm run setup` without `--qa`. Never run `docker compose down -v` on project `moneo`.
- Only test against the QA stack: `npm ci`, then `npm run setup -- --qa` (copies the shared secrets from `~/.moneo/qa.env` and checks migrations), then `npm run qa:auth`. Playwright starts `npm run qa:server` (port 3100) on its own. If port 3100 is already in use by another checkout's QA server, stop and report it rather than killing anything you didn't start.
- No real AI, bank or Scalable calls.

## The problem
1. `e2e/home-dashboard.gated.spec.ts`, test "Home widgets are moved, resized, hidden and added back in place, and stay that way". It fails when Home starts from the **default layout** (delete the QA workspace's `public.dashboard_layouts` row first). Sequence: hide Goals → resize Net worth → Undo → hide Goals again → add another hidden widget → Undo. Goals' heading comes back, but the next `goals.hover()` (~line 102) times out "waiting for element to be visible and stable". That suggests the masonry grid in `app/home-grid.tsx` keeps re-measuring and moving widgets. With leftover layout state it sometimes passed. A patch that adds the layout reset as a `beforeEach` (postgres delete of the QA user's `dashboard_layouts` row, using `SUPABASE_DB_URL` and `E2E_USER_EMAIL` from `.env.qa`) is a good starting point; apply the same idea.
2. `e2e/home-performance.gated.spec.ts` fails: Home CLS is ~0.47 against a 0.1 budget on an empty QA workspace. Layout-shift sources are the widget containers `#spending`, `#overview`, `#budgets` (`div.group relative min-w-0 lg:col-span-*`), at ~4.0 s, 4.7 s and 5.0 s after load as sections stream in.

## What to do
- Reproduce both, find the root cause in the Home grid/masonry and widget loading (use the codebase-design / diagnosing-bugs skills if listed), and fix it in the app, not the specs. Keep the masonry home grid (an owner decision). Reserve space or settle the layout so streaming sections don't push widgets around, and make sure measurement stops once sizes are stable.
- Add the layout reset to `home-dashboard.gated.spec.ts` so it always starts from the default layout. No `test.skip` inside the test; turn the existing `test.skip(at === 0, ...)` into an assertion.
- Verify on a production build too: `E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1 npx playwright test e2e/home-dashboard.gated.spec.ts e2e/home-performance.gated.spec.ts --workers=1`. Run each at least 3 times; all must pass every time. Also check Home on mobile width (390px) and in dark mode with a before/after screenshot, since this is visual.
- Run `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`.
- Commit in steps, in plain language, each ending with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Push and open a PR whose description says what caused it, what you changed, and the checks with numbers (CLS before/after). End it with `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)` and `Closes #185`. Base the PR on `main` if PR #187 is merged by then, otherwise on `t3/qa-stack`.

Report: PR URL, root cause in two sentences, CLS before/after, and how many repeated runs passed.

import io
p='app/home-grid.tsx'
s=io.open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
old='''      const needsContent = !Object.hasOwn(currentWidgets.current, key);
      if (needsContent) setAdding(current => [...current, key]);
      change({ ...current, items }, needsContent);'''
new='''      // Its content may be here now, yet a refresh still on its way from an earlier save (an added widget) carries none,
      // so the restore always brings its own; until then the widget shows its placeholder.
      setAdding(current => current.includes(key) ? current : [...current, key]);
      change({ ...current, items }, true);'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
io.open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
EOF

input.command:
git add app/home-grid.tsx && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Keep a restored Home widget when an earlier refresh lands late

Undo after hiding a widget only asked the server for fresh content when the
widget's content was missing at that moment. If a refresh from an earlier
save (adding another widget) was still on its way, it arrived without the
restored widget, which then vanished and never came back. Undo now always
requests its own refresh and shows the placeholder until it lands.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git add components/chart.tsx app/section-fallback.tsx app/page.tsx && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Stop Home's cash-flow card shifting the grid while it loads

The cash-flow chart loads echarts in a second lazy chunk that renders
nothing meanwhile, so the card collapsed by 240px and grew back, and the
masonry grid moved every widget below it. Its loading placeholder was also
a short "Loading..." card that grew by the chart's height. The chart box now
keeps its height while echarts loads, and the placeholder reserves it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

## What caused it

**Goals vanishing after Undo (the `hover()` timeout).** Undo after hiding a widget asked the server for fresh content only if the widget had no content *at that moment*. In the spec, "add another widget" saves with a refresh; its response can land *after* Undo was clicked. That late refresh carries widgets without Goals, so Goals dropped out of the grid, and because Undo had not asked for its own refresh, it never came back. Playwright saw the node detach repeatedly ("element was detached from the DOM"). It only showed from the default layout, because only then is there another hidden widget to add.

**Layout shift on Home.** The cash-flow chart is lazy twice: `TrendChart` shows a 240px placeholder while the chart module loads, but `CashFlowChart` then renders `ReactECharts`, a second `ssr: false` dynamic import with no placeholder. For ~300 ms the card collapsed from 344px to 104px and grew back, and the masonry grid moved every widget below it (Accounts, Agent team). Its Suspense fallback was also a short "Loading…" card that grew by the chart's height when the data streamed in (most visible on the dev server).

The masonry measurement itself was not looping: the `ResizeObserver` only reacts to real size changes, so once heights stop changing it stops.

## What changed

- `app/home-grid.tsx`: Undo always restores with its own refresh and shows the placeholder until it lands.
- `components/chart.tsx`: the cash-flow chart box has its height while echarts loads.
- `app/section-fallback.tsx`, `app/page.tsx`: the cash-flow fallback reserves the chart's 240px.
- `e2e/home-dashboard.gated.spec.ts`: `beforeEach` deletes the QA user's `dashboard_layouts` row, so every run starts from the default layout. (Main had already replaced the `test.skip(at === 0)`.)

## Checks

Home CLS on an empty QA workspace, measured with a layout-shift observer:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Production build | 0.067 | 0.007 |
| Production, 6× CPU throttle | — | 0.007 |
| Dev server | 0.077 | 0.007–0.027 |

The ~0.47 in the issue was not reproducible here. Its sources (cash flow and the widgets around it) are the ones fixed above. What's left is 0.007 from the masonry spans applying at hydration, plus on dev the Weekly briefing placeholder, which turns into nothing on an empty workspace.

The same specs pass on the dev server 2/2; before the fix the layout test and the phone test failed there.
- Home at 390px (light and dark) and desktop dark: the settled layout is pixel-identical before and after. The change only affects the loading frames.
- `npm test` (1541 passed), `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` all pass.

Closes #185

content.text:
I opened PR #191 against `main` (PR #187 was already merged, so I rebased onto `main` first). Both specs now pass on every run. I could not reproduce the issue's 0.47 CLS on this machine; the shifts I did measure are fixed.

**Root cause:**
- **Goals disappearing:** Undo only asked the server for fresh widget content if the widget had none at the moment you clicked. The refresh from the earlier "add widget" save could arrive after Undo, without Goals in it, so Goals dropped out of the grid and never came back. That is why `hover()` kept finding the element detached. It only happens from the default layout, because only then is there a hidden widget to add.
- **Layout shift:** the cash-flow chart loads the charting library (echarts) through a second lazy import that showed nothing while loading. The card shrank by 240px and grew back about 300ms later, and the masonry grid moved every widget below it. Its loading placeholder was also much shorter than the real card.

The masonry measuring was not looping: it only reacts when a widget's size actually changes, so it stops once sizes settle.

**Fix:**
- Undo now always asks for its own refresh and shows the placeholder until the content arrives.
- The chart box keeps its height while the library loads.
- The cash-flow placeholder reserves the chart's 240px.
- `home-dashboard.gated.spec.ts` now deletes the QA user's `dashboard_layouts` row in a `beforeEach`. `main` had already replaced the `test.skip(at === 0)` with a step that moves Goals forward first, so I kept that instead of adding my assertion.

**Home CLS on an empty QA workspace:**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Production build | 0.067 | 0.007 |
| Production, 6× CPU throttle | not measured | 0.007 |
| Dev server | 0.077 | 0.007–0.027 |

What remains:
- **0.007:** the masonry layout applies when the page becomes interactive.
- **Up to 0.02 (dev only):** the Weekly briefing placeholder disappears when an empty workspace has nothing to show. I left it, because removing the placeholder would make the briefing pop in for users who have data.

**Runs:**
- **Production build** (`E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1 npx playwright test e2e/home-dashboard.gated.spec.ts e2e/home-performance.gated.spec.ts --workers=1`): 3 of 3 runs passed before the rebase and 3 of 3 after, 3 tests each time.
- **Dev server:** 2 of 2 runs passed. Before the fix, the layout test and the phone long-press test both failed there.
- **Unit tests, lint, typecheck, build:** `npm test` (1541 passed), `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` all pass.
- **Screenshots:** the settled Home layout looks the same before and after at 390px in light and dark, and on desktop in dark. Only the loading frames change. Screenshots are in `C:\Users\mgsuk\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\316f66f95fff1b12\c974c5ca-b84c-4eeb-8ee2-1249d19751a0\scratchpad\` (for example `before-mobile-dark.png` and `after-mobile-dark.png`).
